clue.text: Parts of the harness that make tracks

definitions.meaning: the straps linking a draught horse's collar to the cart it pulls
marks or signs left behind by something that has passed

explanation.surface: A saddler explains which bits of tack leave marks on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: harness straps, and the marks or vestiges left behind.

clue.text: Ground providing shelter for soft shelled amphibian

indicators.note: one word wraps around another, giving it cover inside itself

parts.note: ground means terrain, a stretch of land
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Some land offers cover to a delicate-shelled water creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft' looks like part of 'soft shelled', but it is P; strictly the creature is a reptile, loosely called amphibian since it lives in and out of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater turtle with a hard shell, living both in water and on land.

clue.text: International rugger player is one mass of bruises

definitions.meaning: a member of New Zealand's national rugby union team, named for their dark kit
covered entirely in dark bruising, as if beaten all over

explanation.surface: A battered rugby international after a hard match.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand's rugby team wears dark kit; someone completely bruised is dark-coloured everywhere.

clue.text: Always in reverse whichever way you look at it

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the single clue word that follows

explanation.surface: Something holds true forever, whichever direction one approaches it from.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'reverse', and 'whichever way you look at it' adds that it also sits inside the word written backwards (ESREVER).
explanation.definitionFit: Ever is a poetic synonym of forever or at all times.

clue.text: Consonant with the way a buccaneer would act

parts.note: as means in the manner or way that
a buccaneer is a pirate of the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Behaviour fitting how a sea-robber would behave.
explanation.walkthrough: An aspirate is the breathed H sound, a consonant in phonetics.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the breathy sound of H is called by this name, so it is a consonant.

clue.text: Skill which is instinctive and not evolved in safe surroundings

indicators.note: the outer word forms a ring around the other letters placed within it

parts.note: safe means secure

indicators.note: evolved means developed into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An inborn talent that didn't develop but grew up in a protected setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolved' rearranges AND NOT into ONDNAT, and 'surroundings' puts that inside SECURE, between SEC and URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit so ingrained it feels inborn, done without thinking.

clue.text: Terrible king of vain disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful monarch with a conceited temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging; the Russian tsar is known as 'the Terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century Russian tsar is remembered by the epithet the Terrible.

clue.text: The sort of effort a fielding captain calls for

definitions.text: The sort of effort a fielding captain calls for

parts.words: The sort of effort a fielding captain calls for
parts.note: a total, maximum effort, and also what a cricket captain whose side is fielding wants: every batter dismissed

explanation.surface: A cricket captain urging his fielders on.
explanation.definitionFit: Means total or maximum, and in cricket it describes a whole batting side dismissed.

clue.text: Desire ragout of ducks

indicators.note: a ragout is a stewed mixture, so the letters of the word are stirred up

explanation.surface: A craving for a stew made of waterfowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Large sea ducks prized for their soft down.

clue.text: Outstanding claim for a painkiller

definitions.meaning: standing out from a surface, as raised carving does
what a pain-killing drug promises to give: easing of suffering

explanation.surface: An advert boasting that its pills are excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised work in sculpture, and the easing of pain that a drug promises.

clue.text: Bob made childish progress at writing apparently

definitions.text: Bob made childish progress at writing apparently

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
a baby moves forward by crawling on hands and knees

explanation.surface: A toddler named Bob learning to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is a shilling (S, from the Latin solidus) in Britain's old pre-1971 coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrote in a careless, untidy hand, like a child.

clue.text: Postponing playing a ball so hard it goes into the bunker

definitions.meaning: delaying something until later

definitions.text: playing a ball so hard it goes into the bunker
definitions.meaning: a golfer hitting a ball on the green so hard it runs off into the sand trap

explanation.surface: A golfer delaying a shot that might overshoot into the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferring; and in golf, striking a ball on the green so it runs off.

clue.text: Returning whence Napoleon returned in good health

indicators.note: returning means the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Napoleon escaped from exile on the Mediterranean island of Elba in 1815

explanation.surface: A history note about the place from which Napoleon came back healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Able-bodied means fit and strong, physically capable.

clue.text: Peculiar description of a comedian

definitions.meaning: strange or odd
a comic makes people laugh, so is amusing

explanation.surface: Calling a comic odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strange and amusing, as a comic is.

clue.text: How quiet engines run when turning up by car

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is placed beside the other
turning means the small word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a luxury car

explanation.surface: Motoring talk about smooth engines on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses UP to PU, and 'by' sets RR (Rolls-Royce) beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth engine makes a low contented hum, like a cat.

clue.text: Sleepy sound from the South Bank ofthe Thames

parts.note: the Nore is a sandbank in the Thames estuary

explanation.surface: A drowsy noise heard on London's riverside arts district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Bank' looks like the London arts area; it splits into S plus the Nore, a sandbank at the mouth of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy breathing during sleep.

clue.text: Road vehicle has to move like a boat

definitions.meaning: a low electric delivery van, as in milk ..., or a parade vehicle
drift on the surface of water

explanation.surface: A car that has to behave like a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is the small electric van British milkmen drove on morning rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk van or parade cart, and to drift on the water's surface.

clue.text: Never out in a fickle manner

definitions.meaning: read as two words, at home all the time
changeably, unfaithfully

explanation.surface: A capricious person who never goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is always at home; as one it means changeably.

clue.text: The part of horse racing which is not crooked

definitions.meaning: the home stretch of a racecourse before the finish
honest, or without bends

explanation.surface: Praise for an honest bit of the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: The final level stretch of a racecourse, and honest or without bends.

clue.text: Welcome order for riflemen waiting for weapon inspection

definitions.meaning: a warm reception, as in greeting someone gladly

definitions.text: order for riflemen waiting for weapon inspection
definitions.meaning: a drill command to soldiers to show their guns for checking

explanation.surface: A parade-ground scene before a rifle check.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm reception, and a drill command to present guns.

clue.text: Carry light breakfast to work and finish it off

parts.note: carry means bring
toast is a light breakfast
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Taking toast to the office and eating it all up.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, Latin for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something completely, ending it.

clue.text: Lucky charm for many going to the race course

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: Lots of racegoers bringing good-luck tokens.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the English racecourse that hosts Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A token or figure believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: What the patrolman shouted when he saw John steal the lorry

parts.note: a greeting shouted out: hi
Jack is a familiar form of John

explanation.surface: A policeman greets a man who is making off with a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a traditional pet name for John; the greeting plus name runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize a vehicle in transit by force.

clue.text: It may raid this sort of house party

definitions.text: It may raid this sort of house party

parts.words: It may raid this sort of house party
parts.note: police may raid a rave held to a certain style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Police busting a rave.
explanation.walkthrough: A drugs raid on a rave of the late-1980s dance-music style is the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a late-1980s electronic dance genre, and slang for LSD.

clue.text: In the seat of Irish kings one finds the crown of their queens

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Hill of Tara was the seat of the High Kings of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Inside an ancient royal site lies a queen's headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: TARA is the hill in County Meath where Ireland's High Kings were crowned.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headdress worn by royalty.

clue.text: What the tale-telling cotton miller spun

definitions.text: What the tale-telling cotton miller spun

parts.words: What the tale-telling cotton miller spun
parts.note: a mill spins thread, and a storyteller spins a long tale

explanation.surface: A mill worker who tells stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun thread, and a long rambling story.

clue.text: Appeal to a big noise in Asgard

definitions.text: Appeal to a big noise in Asgard

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Praying to an important god in Norse heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Asgard is the home of the Norse gods; 'big noise' also means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse myth, ruling from Asgard.

clue.text: The others don't work

definitions.meaning: the remainder
relax or take a break

explanation.surface: Complaining that everybody else is idle.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder, and to relax.

clue.text: Measure of coal with which a peer heartened the ferryman

indicators.note: heartened means given a heart, so a piece goes into the middle

parts.note: Charon ferried souls across the Styx in Greek myth
LD, short for Lord, is a peer

explanation.surface: A nobleman encouraging a boatman with some coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartened' looks like encouraged; it puts LD into CHARON.
explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of volume for coal, about 36 bushels.

clue.text: Cash book with dividing line between left and right

indicators.note: between means the piece sits in the middle of the two others

parts.note: an edge is a boundary line

explanation.surface: An accounts book ruled into left and right columns.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of accounts in which transactions are recorded.

clue.text: A bowler should be for a lady, but surely not for a maiden

definitions.text: A bowler should be for a lady, but surely not for a maiden

parts.words: A bowler should be for a lady, but surely not for a maiden
parts.note: a gentleman removes his bowler hat for a lady; in cricket a bowler who sends down a maiden over (no runs) would not be dropped from the attack

explanation.surface: Etiquette about hats for ladies and maidens.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so a bowler is rewarded, not removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Removed, as a hat lifted or a bowler replaced.

clue.text: Rank socially acceptable in statistics

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: stats is short for statistics
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Social standing measured in figures.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage, hence acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or position in society.
